title: New York's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for New York's 2nd Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Andrew Garbarino against Democratic challenger Patrick Halpin. The district covers the South Shore of Long Island, including the towns of Babylon, Islip, most of Brookhaven in Suffolk County, and Massapequa in Nassau County. Garbarino, first elected in 2020, chairs the House Homeland Security Committee and is regarded as a moderate Republican who has occasionally broken with his party on high-profile votes. Halpin, a former Suffolk County Executive and current chair of the Suffolk County Water Authority, is making his first run for Congress after decades in local and county government. Nonpartisan analysts rate the race as Solid Republican, reflecting the district's conservative voting history with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+6.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls specific to the NY-02 general election matchup were found as of June 2026. One social media post from the Halpin campaign referenced a tied race, but the campaign itself noted that figure appeared to be a modeled national projection rather than an independent district-level poll.

candidates.name: Andrew Garbarino
candidates.summary: Andrew Garbarino is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. He chairs the House Homeland Security Committee and also serves on the Financial Services and Ethics Committees. A moderate Republican, Garbarino has voted with Democrats on legislation such as the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and the Respect for Marriage Act, and he was one of 35 House Republicans who voted to establish the January 6 commission.

candidates.name: Patrick Halpin
candidates.summary: Patrick Halpin is the Democratic nominee for New York's 2nd Congressional District and a former Suffolk County Executive, having served from 1988 to 1991 as the youngest county executive in Suffolk history. He previously served in the New York State Assembly and on the Suffolk County Legislature. Halpin currently chairs the Suffolk County Water Authority and the Town of Babylon Planning Board, and he is making his first bid for Congress at age 73, emphasizing affordability, public safety, and environmental protection.

forecast.rationale: No independent public district-level polls exist for NY-02 as of June 2026, so this forecast relies entirely on structural indicators. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+6 and nonpartisan analysts rate the race as 'Solid Republican.' Incumbent Andrew Garbarino has held the seat since 2020 and chairs the House Homeland Security Committee. His moderate, occasionally bipartisan record may help retain crossover support in this Long Island district. Democratic nominee Patrick Halpin is a former Suffolk County Executive and a credible local figure, which prevents the race from being a pure safe seat, but he faces an uphill race in a district that leans 6 points more Republican than the national average. Without any district-level polling, confidence remains medium. The rating of 'likely_r' (approximately 90% Republican win probability) reflects a clear but not overwhelming Republican advantage, factoring in incumbency, the R+6 lean, and Halpin's local stature.
